Autocorrelation of the residuals within groups

Source: R/corStruct.R
corStruct.Rd

Correlation structures for the residuals of the observations of a curve over time, for the correlation argument of gcTMB, with the same arguments and the same parameterisation as corAR1 and corCAR1 of the package nlme (whose objects gcTMB also accepts).

Usage

corAR1(value = 0, form = ~1, fixed = FALSE)

corCAR1(value = 0.2, form = ~1, fixed = FALSE)

Arguments

value

Numeric. The starting value of rho, or its value with fixed=TRUE: between -1 and 1 (default 0) for corAR1, between 0 and 1 (default 0.2) for corCAR1

form

One-sided formula. The time covariate and the grouping factor, ~ time | group. Without a grouping factor, the residuals of all observations form a single series when the model has no random effects, and are grouped by the innermost grouping factor of the random effects (the one with most levels) otherwise, as in nlme::lme. Without a time covariate (~ 1 or ~ 1 | group), the times are the positions of the observations within their group.

fixed

Logical. If TRUE, rho is fixed at value and not estimated

Value

An object of class c("corAR1", "corStruct") or c("corCAR1", "corStruct"): value on the unconstrained scale of nlme, log((1 + rho)/(1 - rho)) for AR(1) and log(rho/(1 - rho)) for CAR(1), with the attributes formula and fixed.

Details

The residuals of different groups are independent. Within a group, the residuals e are stationary, with the residual variance sigma^2 of the model (sigma^2/w for weights w) and the correlation $$cor(e_s, e_t) = rho^{|t - s|},$$ with rho the correlation of residuals one unit of time apart (Zuur et al., 2009, Section 6.1; Pinheiro and Bates, 2000, Section 5.3):

  • corAR1: the autoregressive process of order 1 at integer times (positions), with -1 < rho < 1; gaps in the times are allowed, e.g. measurements every second day with form = ~ day | plant and a day without measurement, with the correlation rho^2 across a gap of two days. Without a time covariate (form = ~ 1 | plant), the time is the position of the observation within its group, in the order of the data;

  • corCAR1: the continuous-time autoregressive process of order 1, for times that need not be integers and unequally spaced observations, with 0 < rho < 1.

The times must be unique within a group. As the process is Markov, the likelihood is the product of the density of the first residual of each group and the conditional densities of each residual given the previous one, normal with mean rho^dt e_prev and variance sigma^2 (1 - rho^(2 dt)) for the time dt between them, which is exact and linear in the number of observations.

The estimated parameter is in coef(fit) as cor_par:AR1 or cor_par:CAR1, on the unconstrained scale of nlme (coef of an nlme corStruct): the logit link log(rho/(1 - rho)) for CAR(1), and log((1 + rho)/(1 - rho)), the logit of (1 + rho)/2, for AR(1), whose rho lies between -1 and 1. Wald intervals are computed on this scale and transformed back. corpars gives rho, and confint(fit, parm="cor_par:CAR1") an interval for rho. If nlme is attached after gcTMB, its constructors mask these; gcTMB accepts their objects, and gcTMB's correlation structures can be passed to nlme::gls, nlme::gnls, nlme::lme and nlme::nlme.

References

Pinheiro, J.C. and Bates, D.M. (2000). Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS. Springer, New York.

Zuur, A.F., Ieno, E.N., Walker, N.J., Saveliev, A.A. and Smith, G.M. (2009). Mixed Effects Models and Extensions in Ecology with R. Springer, New York.

See also

gcTMB, corpars for the estimate of rho, and residuals(fit, type="normalized") for residuals that are independent under the model.

Examples

FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
fit <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25,
             correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | plant_ID))
corpars(fit)
#>       rho 
#> 0.9593852
